extracted.intended_audience: authors, publishers, librarians, and readers interested in children's and young-adult literary awards
extracted.subtask_description: Information about the Boston Globe–Horn Book Awards: purpose, categories, eligibility windows, submission rules, timing, and special citations for children's and young-adult books. Useful for potential submitters and researchers of award history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: "Awarded for 'excellence in literature for children and young adults'"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The official wording identifies "excellence in literature for children and young adults" as the standard the award recognizes; no further formalized evaluative subcriteria are given on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award categories
rubrics_metrics.description: One book is recognized in each of four categories: Fiction and Poetry, Nonfiction, and Picture Book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page describes category structure and notes historical changes (see category-history entry). Each category yields a single winner (and sometimes honors).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility period / calendar
rubrics_metrics.description: The Awards follow a school-year calendar. Taking the 2011–2012 cycle for illustration: books published June 2011 to May 2012 were eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility is tied to a June–May publication window (school year) rather than a calendar year; examples on the page illustrate the publication window for a cycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission rules and who may submit
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions from publishers were accepted until May 15; generally the books under consideration have been submitted by their publishers but the panel of judges may honor any eligible book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page notes that publishers typically submit candidates and that there is a firm submission deadline (May 15 in the cited cycle). It also emphasizes judges' discretion to honor eligible books even if not submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publisher submission limits (historical)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before 2011–2012 the publishers were permitted to submit only a limited number of candidates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a historical procedural restriction on the number of submissions allowed per publisher; the page indicates this policy changed after 2011–2012.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of award announcements
rubrics_metrics.description: The awards and honors were announced during June (when U.S. school years end), only one to twelve months after the eligible books were released.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page links the awards' announcement timing to the school-year cycle and gives a typical lag between publication and announcement (one to twelve months).

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Citations
rubrics_metrics.description: There have been five "Special Citations": fourth awards conferred in five different years from 1977 to 1999.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Occasionally the panel has issued an extra recognition (a Special Citation) in addition to the regular category winners; the page lists years/examples where this occurred.
